title: Microseism Trend vs Storm Surf
dataSources: Seismograph events (`seismograph:event`), seismic noise (`seismograph:noise`), air quality (`airquality:reading`), radiation counts (`radiation:count`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), phenology observations (`phenology:observation`), and weather-station rainfall (`weatherstation:reading`).
app: Citizen-science telemetry from seismographs, weather stations, air-quality monitors, Geiger counters, lightning feeds, and phenology journals streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, APIs, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=seismograph:noise
| timechart span=1d avg(microseism_db) as microseism_db avg(wind_kph) as wind_kph
description: Compares long-period microseism energy against wind and storm conditions to reveal the signature of distant surf and weather.
value: Microseism trends turn a home seismograph into a broader environmental sensor, linking geology hobby data with local weather.
implementation: Capture daily noise-floor summaries and enrich them with local wind or swell context from your weather feed.
visualization: Dual-axis line chart of microseism level and wind speed.
grandmaExplanation: It warns how the steady background earth rumble rises and falls with stormy conditions far away.
